newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Red October to improve sales, advertising.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Red October to improve sales, advertising.

text.p: Russia's biggest confectioner, Red October, unwrapped plans on Tuesday to revamp its sales system and launch an advertising campaign after a fall in profits and a loss of appetite for some of its products.

"The main issue now is to change the current sales methods, which do not correspond to the current environment," company President Anatoly Daursky told a news conference. "Look at Mars -- you will see a Sneakers in every kiosk."

Red October's 1996 pre-tax profit fell to 168 billion roubles ($29.3 million) from 185 billion roubles in 1995. Production volume edged down to 57,223 tonnes from 58,906 tonnes, the company said in a statement.
Six percent of production is exported to the United States, Germany, Israel and Mongolia. Daursky said the company planned to raise exports to 10-15 percent in the future.
Daursky said most of Red October's sales were in Moscow and the Moscow region, leaving most of the rest of Russia uncovered.
The company had already signed agreements to sell its goods in eight other Russian cities and would increase the number of shops it has in Moscow, he said.
Daursky also said the company, set up in the last century and once a purveyor to the tsar, had hired Russian advertising agency Premier SV to create an advertising campaign for it.
"We are launching a powerful advertising campaign in August or later, when our competitors are out of breath, " he said.
For the first time in decades, Red October had carried out marketing and management research on its activities under market conditions, Daursky said.
Three years ago Red October carried out Russia's first public share offer, which had limited success, with many people buying shares as souvenirs.

Red October later became the target of Russia's first hostile take-over by one of the country's biggest banks, Bank Menatep. The bid failed because Red October employees, at that time the biggest shareholders, refused to sell their shares.
Daursky said the company planned to make its first preferred shares issue and a Eurobond issue this year and would use the funds raised from the issues to modernise equipment.
In addition to the flagship factory in Moscow, Red October has smaller factories in the central Russian town of Ryazan and is building a new factory in Kolomna.
It has also bought 40 percent of a confectioner in the southern city of Tambov and 30 percent in a Tula factory.
The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development is extending he company a $15 million loan under "civilised interest", Daursky said.
